title: Cost, intelligence and speed tags — pick a design

steps.path: The model list: New Session, or the model name in the status bar
steps.headline: Which layout should the tags use? Hover or press any tag to see the figures behind it.
steps.risk: Every price and score is real, taken 11 September. The two estimated speeds (the ~ tags) are made up for the preview; the others are your own measurements.

variants.label: Chips under the name
variants.summary: Words on a second line, each on a softly coloured chip. Every row becomes two lines tall.
variants.measured: Rows 53 px tall, up from 33 today
variants.risk: In a narrow window a row with three tags (a downloaded model) wraps its speed tag onto a third line.

variants.label: Dots under the name
variants.summary: The same words on a second line, each behind a coloured dot, with no chip outline. Quieter; the colour is smaller.
variants.measured: Rows 47 px tall, up from 33 today
variants.risk: The dot is about 5 px wide, so good and bad are harder to spot and colour is the only signal; the hollow "Not rated" dot nearly disappears on the Light theme.

variants.label: Short, beside the name
variants.summary: Short forms on the same line at the right: rows stay one line tall, but long names are cut off, and your "SUBSCRIPTION PLAN" and "FREE - LOCAL" shrink to "Plan" and "Free".
variants.risk: Names are cut sooner: "Qwen3.6 35B A3B" shows as "Qwen3.6 35B A3…".

steps.path: The cost tag on a plan model, and on a model on this computer
steps.headline: Should the plan and local tags keep your capitals, or be written like the other tags?
steps.today: On the first questions page you wrote these tags as SUBSCRIPTION PLAN and FREE - LOCAL, and the mockups use exactly that. The other tags are written normally: Poor value, Mid price, Intelligence 84.
steps.problem: A tester who had never seen the app read the capitals and the hyphen as inconsistent with the tags beside them, and suggested plainer words.
steps.proposal: Three answers. The colours and layout stay as you pick above.

options.label: Keep your capitals
pros: The two tags that mean no charge per use stand out from the price tags.
cons: Reads as shouting next to the other tags.

options.label: Same words, normal case
pros: Your words, written the way every other tag is.
cons: Less emphasis on the two tags that mean no charge per use.

options.label: The tester's wording
options.summary: "In your plan" and "Free · on this computer".
pros: Says plainly what each means to someone new.
cons: "Free · on this computer" is the longest tag, so a downloaded model's row would wrap onto a third line.

steps.path: Hovering or pressing an intelligence tag
steps.headline: Scores come from Epoch AI's index; hovering adds DeepSWE coding, GPQA science, SimpleQA facts and LMArena instruction following.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: this is what you agreed in chat on 11 September, put on the record here. All four are free to reuse with credit; results Epoch copied from company sites (Cursor, WebDev Arena) are left out.
steps.notice: Every hover names its sources and the date of the scores.

steps.path: Hover hints inside the model list and the project list
steps.headline: Hover hints now show above pop-up lists instead of hidden behind them.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: a hint opened inside the model list or the project list was drawn underneath the list, so "Add to favourites" on the model list's star never appeared. Hints now sit on top of everything; they can never block a click.
steps.notice: Hints you have never seen before appear in those two lists.
